standard_prerequisites.name: Faithful functor
standard_prerequisites.statement: A functor is faithful when its action on each hom-type is injective.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the conclusion: precomposition with H must be injective on hom-types of functor precategories.

standard_prerequisites.name: Essentially surjective functor
standard_prerequisites.statement: H is essentially surjective when for every b there merely exists an a with H a = b.
standard_prerequisites.use: It lets one assume a preimage and an isomorphism at source line 1382.

standard_prerequisites.name: Naturality of a natural transformation
standard_prerequisites.statement: A natural transformation commutes with the action of functors on morphisms.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is what turns the middle equality of the displayed chain into the conjugation formula.

core_obligations: Reduce the goal to showing gamma = delta for natural transformations gamma, delta : F -> G with gamma H = delta H, and then to gamma_b = delta_b for an arbitrary b (source lines 1380-1381).
Note that the goal is a mere proposition, so by essential surjectivity of H one may assume a point a and an isomorphism f : H a = b (source line 1382).

Conclude by the displayed chain gamma_b = G(f) o gamma_{H a} o F(inv f) = G(f) o delta_{H a} o F(inv f) = delta_b, in which the two outer equalities are naturality of gamma and delta applied to f, and the middle equality is the hypothesis gamma H = delta H (source lines 1383-1387).

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce to components and strip the essential surjectivity.
Compare the components by the conjugation chain.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 9.9.1 at source lines 1376-1378: if H is an essentially surjective functor then precomposition with H is faithful. The author's proof (source lines 1379-1388) is short but it is a genuine conjugation argument: after reducing to the equality of two components at an arbitrary object b (lines 1380-1381), the proof uses that the goal is a mere proposition to strip the truncation in essential surjectivity and obtain a preimage with an isomorphism f : H a = b (line 1382), and then the two components are identified through the composite G(f) o (-) o F(inv f), where naturality of the two transformations provides the outer equalities and the hypothesis gamma H = delta H provides the middle one (lines 1383-1387). The statement mentions only the two named notions; the conjugation formula is invisible in it.
